title: SOC2 heuristic scratch: control mapping & quick evidence plan
content:
Purpose / quick intent:
- Brain dump for mapping high-risk flows to SOC2 CC controls, quick evidence checklist to hand to infra/platform owners. Not polished — notes to self.

Quick context:
- Focus: CC6 (change management), CC7 (logical access), CC3 (system operations), CC2 (communication/monitoring). Hosted + Dedicated + Private footprints — slightly different owners.
- Goal this sprint: get 6 control owners to confirm evidence sources and provide a sample artifact by end of week 2.

High-level control mapping (working heuristic):
- Deploy approvals & code review -> CC6. Evidence: GitHub PRs, merge checks, protected-branch logs, release notes. Owner: infra-release.
- Provisioning of infra (AWS/GCP) -> CC3/CC7. Evidence: Terraform state versions, CloudTrail Create/Update events, IAM role change logs. Owner: platform-eng.
- Key management for customer keys -> CC7. Evidence: KMS audit logs, HSM access exceptions. Owner: security-crypto.
- Access reviews for admin consoles -> CC7. Evidence: quarterly access-review spreadsheets, Okta reports. Owner: identity-team.
- Incident detection & response -> CC3/CC2. Evidence: pager duty timelines, Postmortems, alert runbooks. Owner: sre.

Questions to confirm with owners (short):
- What is canonical evidence for PR approvals? (Are 'squash merges' logged with reviewer metadata?)
- Where are Terraform state backups kept and who can access them?
- Do we have a retention policy on CloudTrail logs (S3 bucket + lifecycle)?
- Who runs quarterly access review and is there an audit trail for sign-off?
- For Dedicated customers: separate VPCs—how are network change approvals recorded?

Evidence quick checklist (ask owners to attach samples):
- 1x PR showing reviewer + merge protection enforced (screenshot + PR link).
- 1x Terraform apply plan + state change (timestamped).
- 2 weeks of CloudTrail S3 objects showing Create/Update events around infra changes.
- Okta admin export for last month showing admin role changes.
- Example of a customer-facing communication for a maintenance window (email or status page entry).

Notes to self: how to get these quickly without heavy asks
- Use API exports first: GH REST API for PR + branch protection, Terraform Cloud API if used, cloud provider APIs for CloudTrail S3 listing.
- If owner resists, offer to run the export and redact sensitive bits. Quick redaction script: jq + scrub list (ips, account ids).

Potential red flags (call these out to manager):
- No branch protection on a handful of repos used by infra team -> high risk.
- Terraform state accessible by too many principals.
- CloudTrail retention less than 90 days for infra events.

Triage play for first owner sync (15m agenda):
- 2m: state the ask + deadline.
- 5m: confirm canonical sources (APIs, dashboards, buckets).
- 5m: agree on a sample artifact to provide.
- 3m: assign next steps + owner.

Mini action list (this doc = source for handoffs):
- [ ] Draft a short email template to request evidence (include exact API commands).
- [ ] Create a small script to pull PR + branch-protection info (GH token scope = repo:status).
- [ ] Reach out to platform-eng on Terraform state owners. (Assigned to Marta)
- [ ] Collect Okta admin export (Assigned to Noah)

API snippets to include in email (notes):
- GitHub: GET /repos/:org/:repo/pulls/:number -> reviewer + merged_by fields
- AWS: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=CreateStack
- Okta: /api/v1/reports/system_log?since=2026-02-01 (filter for user.admin.role.update)

Open design questions / follow-ups:
- Do Dedicated deployments have separate audit log sinks or are they aggregated into the same logging pipeline? (If separate, we need signed assertions for retention policies)
- Do we have a canonical definition of who is "admin" vs "operator" across teams? Varied naming is making sample artifacts noisy.

Quick draft email template (for 1:1 owner ask):
"Hey <OWNER>,
We are pulling together SOC2 evidence for control area <CONTROL>. Could you provide one canonical sample artifact that shows the control in operation (suggested: PR link, CloudTrail snippet, Okta export) for the period Feb 1–Mar 1 2026? If you prefer, I can run the export and redact sensitive fields. Target: share by EOD Thu. Thanks — Luca."

Last bits:
- Keep lightweight: auditors want traceability not perfect formatting. One clear artifact + statement of where/how it's generated is often sufficient.
- Log everything of the handoffs in a single confluence page (CONFLUENCE-5462) so reviewers don't lose context.

TODOs for next session (Mar 10 sync):
- Confirm 6 owners + their sample artifacts.
- Run automated script for GH + CloudTrail exports (iterate until artifacts match expected fields).
- Draft control narratives for CC6 + CC7 (short paragraphs).

End-of-doc quick notes:
- Save a copy of any sample artifact to internal evidence bucket with a hashed filename and access controls.
- If anything looks off, escalate to Emma (Head of Trust) — better to flag early.

Random thought: consider a "starter evidence kit" repo with scripts + README for each owner category (infra, identity, release). Could speed things next quarter.

-- Luca
